editorial_corrections: Transcript repeatedly says multinomial where discussion is multivariate Normal; preserve correct distribution distinctions.
Mean-variance calculations require finite second moments, not Normality as a mathematical necessity.
w-transpose Sigma w is variance, not volatility.

First-difference L1 penalty on returns gives piecewise constant fits; it penalizes total variation, not the literal number of sign switches. Second-difference L1 trend filtering gives piecewise linear fits.
Full-sample trend smoothing and HMM smoothed probabilities use future observations. Forward HMM filtering is causal only if its fitted parameters are also available at the decision time.
Scenario moment identity is exact for the same weighted finite scenarios. Random finite Gaussian draws only approximate externally specified moments; Normality is not needed for the identity.
Mixture covariance includes between-regime mean differences; matching just the average covariance omits risk.

Lecture and lab differ on spending trigger thresholds, loss thresholds, and monthly versus quarterly transitions. Original example must specify its own period and conventions instead of reproducing incompatible numbers.
Simulation can reveal sensitivity under assumptions; a two-regime model is not necessarily more accurate than a one-regime model in empirical use.
Withdrawals are cash flows, not negative investment returns; distinguish real terminal shortfall, drawdown and sequence risk.
